learning_outcomes:
1.  |  Undergraduate Study
Upon completion of this
Programme, students will have acquired:
Knowledge outcomes
(1)  |  Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra;
(2)  |  Analysis which includes Calculus,
Real Analysis, Complex Analysis, Fourier Analysis and Functional Analysis;
(3)  |  Differential Geometry;
(4)  |  Computer programming for Mathematics
and Numerical Analysis; and
(5)  |  Physics which includes classic
mechanics, electromagnetism, fluids, waves, optics, and quantum mechanics
Skills outcomes
Generic Competencies
(1)  |  An ability to understand broad mathematical literature
independently;
(2)  |  An awareness of mathematical problems arising in generic
situations;
(3)  |  An ability to communicate mathematical problems effectively;
(4)  |  An ability to formulate mathematical problems and know how to find
ways to solve them; and
(5)  |  An ability to solve real-life problems with mathematical software.
Sectors of Professional Skills
In addition, students will
have possessed professional skills in at least one sector:
(1)  |  Postgraduate research
(2)  |  Teaching
(3)  |  Interdisciplinary research between mathematics and other
scientific disciplines
Value and attitudes
outcomes
(1)  |  An ability to apply their mathematical knowledge generically in
their future profession in a way that is unique for mathematically trained
experts; and
(2)  |  An ability to make important original contributions in
mathematical sciences and lead breakthrough of interdisciplinary
mathematical-science applications.
Advanced Learning
Opportunity
(1)  |  An ability to take the Candidacy Examination for the Ph.D. programme of the Articulated Bachelor of Science - Ph.D. Programme in Mathematical
Sciences (ABP).
(2)  |  An ability to transit into the Ph.D. programme of ABP Programme.
(3)  |  An ability to prepare research proposal and decide the research
topics in the Ph.D. programme of ABP Programme.
2.  |  Research Postgraduate Study
(1)  |  Our research programme aims to nurture talented and committed
students who have the capability and aspiration to embark on careers that
would allow them to become world leaders in mathematical sciences to
contribute to the development of Hong Kong, the Country, and the
international community.
(2)  |  The University expects doctoral degree graduates of research
programmes to have acquired in-depth knowledge in a number of major areas of an academic discipline while
maintaining a broad understanding of other related fields. Doctoral degree
graduates should have accumulated enough educational experience and
background learning to be capable of performing independent research to
advance scholarship, with global standards. In particular, doctoral graduates
should have the ability to identify research trends and opportunities,
venture into new research areas when appropriate, define long-term research
objectives, formulate original research problems, and originate and develop
solution methodologies. Doctoral graduates should be capable of producing
research output at a level that can either lead to publications in
high-ranking scholastic venues, or to novel applications in relevant
industrial, commercial, or other public sectors, or to other forms of useful
knowledge transfer to society. They should have gained proficiency in
techniques of knowledge dissemination through presentation and writing and
some teaching experiences through student tutoring.
(3)  |  For graduates of research programmes at doctoral level,
communication and language skills at a level appropriate to university
graduates are expected already at the time of admission. In particular,
fluent communication skills are expected in the language(s) essential to
their research areas. In general, a high level of proficiency in English is
expected as it is commonly regarded as the default international research
language. Ability in a second language is encouraged.
(4)  |  Graduates of the ABP Programme will build collaborations between
physics, computer science and engineering through the application of advanced
mathematical techniques. They will bridge the gap between mathematics and
innovative applications. They will drive breakthroughs at the interface
between theory and practice by combining deep mathematical rigor with the
communicative agility to lead interdisciplinary teams. The ABP Programme's
accelerated course of study ensures that graduates excel in both specialized
research and interdisciplinary problem-solving, preparing them to tackle
complex challenges in academia and industry.

Bachelor of Science in Mathematical Sciences
Major Programme Requirement
Students are required to
complete a minimum of 71 units of courses as follows:
Units
1.  |  Faculty Package:  |  9
IMSC1113,
1122, 2028
2.  |  Required Courses:  |  41
(a)  |  IMSC1038, 2018, 2041, 2048, 2058, 2068, 2078[a] or
2240[a], 2230, MATH2221, PHYS3011, 3021, 3031 or 4031, 3041
(b)  |  Capstone course: IMSC4800 or 4900 or MATH4400 or 4900
3.  |  Elective Courses:  |  21
(a)  |  18-21 units of courses to be chosen from mathematics
subject, as listed in (i) and (ii) below:
(i)  |  18-21 units from among:
(1)  |  one course from IMSC3250, MATH4030,
5061;
(2)  |  one course from IMSC3260, MATH3070,
5070;
(3)  |  one course from IMSC3270, MATH4220,
5021, 5022;
(4)  |  one course from IMSC3280, MATH4240;
(5)  |  one course from IMSC3290, MATH3230,
3240, 5211, 5212;
(6)  |  one course from IMSC3300, MATH3320,
3340;
(7)  |  IMSC courses at 4000 or 5000 level,
except IMSC4800, 4900
(ii)  |  0-3 units from (IMSC2078[a] or
MATH5051) or (IMSC2240[a] or MATH4010)
(b)  |  0-3 units of courses to be chosen
from interdisciplinary subjects, as listed in (i), (ii) and (iii) below:
(i)  |  Core computer science and
programming courses: AIST1110, CSCI2100, 3130, 3160
(ii)  |  Artificial intelligence and machine
learning courses: CSCI3230, 3320
(iii)  |  Information theory and signal
processing courses: MIEG2051, 2440
Total:  |  71
Explanatory Notes:
1.  |  All Faculty Package courses, Required Courses, and
Elective Courses will be included in the calculation of Major GPA for
honours classification.
2.  |  Courses at 5000 and 6000 level completed in
undergraduate study will be automatically recognised to fulfill the
Coursework Requirement for the Ph.D. Programme. No application for course
and unit exemptions is required.
3.  |  Students will be conferred the Bachelor’s degree,
subject to the fulfillment of the undergraduate graduation requirements.
4.  |  To be eligible to proceed with the postgraduate
studies, students are required to satisfy the minimum admission
requirements prescribed by the Graduate School and Zhizhen School after
completion of the fourth year.
5.  |  Students are required to sit for the
Candidacy Examination in their fourth year of attendance, even if
they have not yet completed their undergraduate studies. They have to
pass the Candidacy Examination before the end of the first year of
attendance of postgraduate study to satisfy the Candidacy Examination
requirement for the Ph.D. Programme. Students may attempt to take the
Candidacy Examination in their third year of attendance subject to
approval of the School Director. Students who win individual gold or
silver awards in the Yau College Student Mathematics Competition or
equivalent may apply for exemption from the Candidacy Examination in the
corresponding direction.
6.  |  In order to fulfill the graduation requirements for
postgraduate study, students must complete a minimum of 9 months of
non-local learning/ research experience, with at least 3 consecutive
months of such experience. A formal term-time exchange programme during
undergraduate study, or non-consecutive and substantial non-local
learning/ research experiences of 4 months or more offered by the
University, Colleges, the Faculty of Engineering or Science, Zhizhen
School, the Mathematics Department and other relevant programmes may also
be considered, subject to the approval of the Division Head.
7.  |  A student who wishes to transfer to the programmes
offered by the Faculty of Science or Faculty of Engineering, or relevant
programmes of other Faculties shall follow the prevailing rules and
regulations of the University and obtain prior permission from the School
Director through written application. Such applications should be made
one month before the commencement of designated application period for
change of programme. No such application shall be accepted once the
application period has commenced. In general, students must apply for a
change of programme no later than the third year of attendance of their
undergraduate studies.
[a]  |  Either one of the two courses taken to fulfill the Required
Courses requirement cannot be used to fulfill the Elective Courses
requirement.
Doctor of Philosophy in Mathematical Sciences
Pre-candidacy
The “candidacy requirement” composes of four major
parts, namely coursework requirement, candidacy examination, thesis
proposal (and oral defence) and stipulated Improving Postgraduate
Learning (IPL) module requirements. Students must complete and fulfill
the four parts within the maximum period stipulated by
the Programme. Details of the requirement are listed below:
Units
1.  |  Coursework Requirement
(a)  |  Lecture courses:  |  15
15 units of MATH or IMSC courses at 5000 and 6000
level, with at least 9 units of these courses covering at least three of
the following directions:
(i)  |  Algebra and Number Theory
IMSC5011, 5012, MATH5051, 5052, 6031, 6032, 6061,
6062
(ii)  |  Analysis and Partial Differential Equations
IMSC5021, 5022, MATH5011, 5012, 5021, 5022, 6041,
6042, 6081, 6082
(iii)  |  Computational and Applied Mathematics
IMSC5041, 5042, MATH5211, 5212, 6211, 6212, 6221,
6222, 6231, 6232, 6241, 6242, 6251, 6261
(iv)  |  Geometry and Topology
IMSC5031, 5032, MATH5070, 5031, 5032, 5061, 5062,
6021, 6022, 6051, 6052, 6071, 6072
(b)  |  Thesis research/ monitoring courses:  |  12
Students must register for a Thesis Research course
every term: MATH8006
2.  |  Candidacy Examination
Students need to pass the Candidacy Examination
(written and oral examinations) in 3 directions out of 4. The Candidacy
Examination directions consist of: (a) Algebra and Number Theory, (b) Analysis
and Partial Differential Equations, (c) Computational and Applied
Mathematics, and (d) Geometry and Topology. Those who win individual gold or silver awards in the
Yau College Student Mathematics Competition or equivalent are allowed to
apply for exemption from the Candidacy Examination in the corresponding
direction.
3.  |  Thesis Proposal and Oral Defence
Students must submit a research proposal endorsed by
the supervisor, and pass an oral defence.
4.  |  Improving Postgraduate Learning (IPL) modules:
Students are required to complete and pass the
following Improving Postgraduate Learning (IPL) modules in their first
year of attendance for partial fulfilment of candidacy requirements:
(a)  |  An IPL module on “Basics of Research Data Management” This is an online module and relevant information can
be accessed from the website: https://www.cuhk.edu.hk/clear/download/IPL-Researchskills.pdf.
(b)  |  Students are required to submit a Data Management
Plan (DMP), with effect from the 2025-26 intake.
5.  |  Other Requirements
(a)  |  Students must fulfill the Term Assessment Requirement
of the Graduate School. For details, please refer to Clause 13.0
“Unsatisfactory Performance and Discontinuation of Studies” of the
General Regulations Governing Postgraduate Studies which can be accessed
from the Graduate School Homepage: https://www.gs.cuhk.edu.hk.
Total:  |  27
Remarks:
1.  |  Ph.D. students are
required to fulfill all of the above candidacy requirements [1 to 5] by
the end of the first year of attendance of postgraduate study before
advancement to Ph.D. post-candidacy.
Post-candidacy
Units
1.  |  Coursework Requirement
(a)  |  Thesis research/monitoring courses:  |  72
Students must register for a Thesis Research course
every term: MATH8012 (or MATH8006 for continuing students).
(b)  |  Other course(s):  |  6
Students must take Graduate Seminars course twice:
MATH7400.
2.  |  Non-local learning/research experience
Students must complete a minimum of 9 months of
non-local learning/ research experience, with at least 3 consecutive
months of such experience. A formal term-time exchange programme during
undergraduate study, or non-consecutive and substantial non-local
learning/research experiences of 4 months or more offered by the
University, Colleges, the Faculty of Engineering or Science, the
Mathematics and other relevant programmes may also be considered, subject
to the approval of the Division Head.
3.  |  Improving Postgraduate Learning (IPL) modules:
Students are required to complete the following IPL
modules for graduation:
(a)  |  An IPL module on “Observing Intellectual Property and
Copyright Law during Research”. This is an online module and relevant
information can be accessed from the website: https://www.cuhk.edu.hk/clear/prodev/ipl.html.
(b)  |  An IPL module on “Becoming an Excellent TA: Professional
Development Course for Teaching Assistants”.
(c)  |  Students must complete an online Research Ethics
Training (RET) module on “Publication Ethics” offered by the Office of
Research and Knowledge Transfer Services (ORKTS) and obtain a valid
Publication Ethics Certificate for graduation. Relevant information can
be accessed from the RET website at https://www.research-ethics.cuhk.edu.hk/web/.
(d)  |  The final DMP should have been shared to the CUHK
community on DMP Tool or the relevant platform that CUHK provides
when submitting the final version of the thesis/portfolio to the Graduate
School. Students are required to have published the data on the CUHK
Research Data Repository or an open data repository with a valid Digital
Object Identifier (DOI) or other forms of permanent identifier when
submitting the final version of the thesis/portfolio. Upon thesis
supervisor’s endorsement, students can decide on how much data from the
research project is to be published.
4.  |  Other Requirements
(a)  |  Students must fulfill the Term Assessment Requirement
of the Graduate School. For details, please refer to Clause 13.0
“Unsatisfactory Performance and Discontinuation of Studies” of the
General Regulations Governing Postgraduate Studies which can be accessed
from the Graduate School Homepage: https://www.gs.cuhk.edu.hk.
(b)  |  Students are required to submit a research thesis and
pass an oral defence for graduation.
Total:  |  78
